To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk status of children at the start of first grade was related to their achievement at the end of the year, and that the quality of the instructional and emotional support that children experienced in first grade classrooms moderated this relationship.
the effects of children's risk for school failure can be mitigated through the provision of strong instructional and emotional supports in the first grade.

children who were at risk of school difficulties in kindergarten were less at risk in first grade if they had teachers who provided them with high levels of instructional and emotional support, and that the children who were most at risk of school problems were those who had low support from their first grade teacher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which children s risk of school failure is moderated by support from the classroom environment.
the development of children at risk of academic and social problems in the early school years.
the role of the school in children's lives and how it affects children's development, particularly children who have multiple difficulties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study suggest that the classroom context can play an important role in moderating the effects of early childhood risk factors.
children at risk of failure in school may benefit from the instructional and emotional support provided in first grade classrooms.
, for at risk children, the quality of the classroom is an important moderator of the risk of school failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classroom environment can make a big difference for children at-risk of school failure, but that this effect is not universal for all children.

the quality of the classroom environment can make a big difference for children at-risk of school failure, but the effects of the classroom environment on children's development are mediated by children's individual characteristics.
the quality of the teacher-student relationship is an essential component of the classroom experience that can have a positive impact on children at risk of academic difficulties and school failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers can make a difference in children’s lives.
teachers and other school personnel can make a difference for students at risk of school problems.
the quality of the classroom matters.
